items.title: Llama cpp should be pre-installed when creating a worker
items.body:
<!-- Thanks for helping us to improve LocalAI! We welcome all bug reports. Please fill out each area of the template so we can better help you. Comments like this will be hidden when you post but you can delete them if you wish. -->

**LocalAI version:**
<!-- Container Image or LocalAI tag/commit -->
localai/localai:latest-gpu-nvidia-cuda-12 (latest)
Same happens with the script-installed local-ai, more info below.
**Environment, CPU architecture, OS, and Version:**
<!-- Provide the output from "uname -a", HW specs, if it's a VM  -->
Linux 6.8.12-13-pve, LXC
x2 RTX 2060
**Describe the bug**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->
When adding a worker with the script or with a docker image, for example with this command:
`docker run -ti --net host -e TOKEN="longtokenFromP2P-server" --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 --gpus all localai/localai:latest-gpu-nvidia-cuda-12 worker p2p-llama-cpp-rpc`

It isn't installing, by default, the llama cpp backend. All workers require llama cpp as mentioned in the documentation, but by default it isn't installing it.


**To Reproduce**
<!-- Steps to reproduce the behavior, including the LocalAI command used, if any -->
Run a P2P server, get the token, then run the same docker image command I mentioned above. In the logs you will see `ERR Failed to find llama-cpp-rpc-server error="llama-cpp backend not found, install it first"`.

**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->
This is expected on a default installation, but when running a worker you absolutely need llama cpp installed. It should be preinstalled.

**Logs**
<!-- If applicable, add logs while running LocalAI in debug mode (`--debug` or `DEBUG=true`) to help explain your problem.  -->

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context about the problem here. -->

items.title: LocalAI P2P connection failure between Linux server and Windows 11 WSL2 instances
items.body:
**LocalAI version:**
localai/localai:v2.20.1-cublas-cuda12-ffmpeg-core

**Environment, CPU architecture, OS, and Version:**
1. Linux server: x86 GPU 2060 12 GB, Docker Ubuntu 22.04
2. Windows 11 PC: x86 WSL2, GPU 4070 12 GB, Docker Desktop (with WSL2) Ubuntu image

**Describe the bug**
Unable to establish P2P connection between LocalAI instances running on a Linux server and a Windows 11 PC with WSL2. The server UI shows 0/0 nodes connected, despite both instances being on the same LAN and able to communicate otherwise

**To Reproduce**
1. Start the LocalAI container on the Windows 11 PC with WSL2 using the provided docker-compose configuration
2. Start the LocalAI container on the Linux server using the provided docker-compose configuration
3. Open the LocalAI server UI
4. Observe that the UI shows 0/0 nodes connected

**Expected behavior**
The LocalAI instances should establish a P2P connection, and the server UI should show at least one connected node

**Logs**
I don't think it's usefull to attach all logs but they mainly say"found node" or "successfully announced"

**Additional context**
1. Both machines are on the same LAN and can communicate with each other for other applications
2. CUDA and NVCC are running correctly on both systems
3. The `llama-cpp-args` parameter is not recognized when trying to set a specific port
4. There might be issues with WSL network port forwarding, but it's unclear as the port can't be set manually
5. Both instances are using the same token for authentication
6. The PC instance is using the `worker p2p-llama-cpp-rpc` command, while the server instance is using `whisper-base` with the `--p2p` flag

items.title: Distributed Llama.cpp Inferencing option `llamacpp-worker` not working
items.body:
<!-- Thanks for helping us to improve LocalAI! We welcome all bug reports. Please fill out each area of the template so we can better help you. Comments like this will be hidden when you post but you can delete them if you wish. -->

**LocalAI version:**
<!-- Container Image or LocalAI tag/commit -->

LocalAI v2.16.0
Docker Image ID: f82868278773 / TAG: latest-aio-cpu

**Environment, CPU architecture, OS, and Version:**
<!-- Provide the output from "uname -a", HW specs, if it's a VM  -->

```
uname -a: Linux XXX 6.5.0-35-generic #35~22.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue May  7 09:00:52 UTC 2 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU D-1521 @ 2.40GHz
RAM: 16 GB
```

**Describe the bug**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

When running `local-ai llamacpp-worker <listening_address> <listening_port>`, local-ai tries to load `llamacpp-worker`, `<listening_address>` and `<listening_port>` as model instead of starting the localai llamacpp-worker.

**To Reproduce**
<!-- Steps to reproduce the behavior, including the LocalAI command used, if any -->

Pull latest latest-aio-cpu image and run it with the `llamacpp-worker` option
Alternatively, start bash terminal inside the container using `docker exec -it local-ai /bin/bash` and run the command `./local-ai llamacpp-worker 0.0.0.0 123445`

**Expected behavior**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->

Should be able to start workers to offload the computation when running:
```
local-ai llamacpp-worker <listening_address> <listening_port>
```

**Logs**
<!-- If applicable, add logs while running LocalAI in debug mode (`--debug` or `DEBUG=true`) to help explain your problem.  -->

```
root@7aadfbf3f809:/build# ./local-ai llamacpp-worker 0.0.0.0 123445

9:59PM INF Setting logging to info

9:59PM WRN [startup] failed resolving model '0.0.0.0'
9:59PM WRN [startup] failed resolving model '123445'
9:59PM INF Preloading models from /build/models
```

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context about the problem here. -->

Trying Distributed Llama.cpp Inferencing after v2.16 release notes
